title: GeneralizedAffineHessianVector.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization on R^d; nonconvex objectives are permitted. The gradient is continuously differentiable, and there exists a global lower bound m with f(x0)-m≤Δ. A minimizer need not exist.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: An independent fresh seed supplies an unbiased gradient g(x), with E‖g(x)-∇f(x)‖^p≤σg^p+αg^p‖∇f(x)‖^p. Queries do not expose the seed or permit its reuse.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedAffineHessianVector.lean: spec.Query, spec.admissible oracle answer, IID and gradient moment clauses

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Unbiased stochastic Hessian-vector products h(x,v), with E‖h(x,v)-∇²f(x)v‖^q≤(σh^q+αh^q‖∇f(x)‖^q)‖v‖^q. Each query requests either one gradient or one Hessian-vector product; both consume the same fixed total oracle budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedAffineHessianVector.lean: spec.Query and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace, Convergence

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: ‖∇²f(x)‖op≤L0+L1‖∇f(x)‖ everywhere, with L0,L1≥0; no Lipschitz Hessian assumption.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedAffineHessianVector.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible Hessian norm clause

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: Separate exponents 1<p≤2 and 1<q≤2 control gradient and Hessian-vector central moments. Their scales may grow with the gradient norm through αg and αh; finite variance is not required when the corresponding exponent is below two. All noise coefficients are nonnegative.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean space R^d with its Euclidean norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Oracle seeds are independent and identically distributed across calls. All Params, including dimension, initial point, accuracy, moment exponents, smoothness and noise bounds, and Δ, are public; f and the oracle distributions are hidden.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Output is a measurable point X in R^d with integrable ‖∇f(X)‖ and E‖∇f(X)‖≤ε, ε>0.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation includes algorithm randomness and the independent oracle sequence; execution uses a fixed upper budget counting all gradient and Hessian-vector calls.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Combines generalized smoothness with separate heavy-tail exponents and gradient-dependent moment scales for independent stochastic gradient and Hessian-vector observations.

descriptionHtml:
Generalized Smoothness with Hessian-Vector Oracles

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d≥0 is an integer. The function f is (L0,L1)-smooth with L0,L1≥0 and has a continuously differentiable gradient. A given point x0∈Rd has objective gap at most Δ≥0 above a global lower bound. The oracle returns either an unbiased stochastic gradient or an unbiased stochastic Hessian-vector product, using independent samples and allowing heavy-tailed, gradient-dependent errors. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈Rd with integrable gradient norm satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, averaging over sampling and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). We use the Euclidean norm ∥⋅∥ and its induced operator norm ∥⋅∥op. Let Ω be a measurable sample space. The noise parameters satisfy σg,αg,σh,αh≥0,1<p≤2,1<q≤2. The algorithm receives d, Ω, L0, L1, σg, αg, σh, αh, p, q, Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Generalized smoothness). The function f is differentiable everywhere, its gradient is continuously differentiable, and ∥∇2f(x)∥op≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥,x∈Rd. Here ∇2f(x) is a linear operator on Rd.

Assumption 2 (Lower bound and initial gap). There exists m∈R such that f(x)≥mfor every x∈Rd,f(x0)−m≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic gradient and Hessian-vector access). There exist a probability measure ν on Ω and jointly measurable maps g:Rd×Ω→Rd,h:(Rd×Rd)×Ω→Rd. For every x,v∈Rd, the random vectors g(x,ξ) and h(x,v,ξ), with ξ∼ν, are Bochner integrable and satisfy Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[h(x,v,ξ)]=∇2f(x)v. Their respective error norms to powers p and q are integrable, with Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥p]≤σgp+αgp∥∇f(x)∥p,Eξ∼ν[∥h(x,v,ξ)−∇2f(x)v∥q]≤(σhq+αhq∥∇f(x)∥q)∥v∥q. At call k, a gradient query at x returns g(x,ξk), while a Hessian-vector query at (x,v) returns h(x,v,ξk). The measurable samples (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent with common law ν, and are independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

Queries may use any x,v∈Rd. Each call requests one of the two replies, and both query types count toward a single oracle-call budget. After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and satisfy EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, with ∥∇f(x¯)∥ integrable under P, the joint law of the samples and the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
On Euclidean Rd, f has a continuously differentiable gradient, f≥m, f(x0)−m≤Δ, and ∥∇2f(x)∥≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥. Jointly measurable, integrable, unbiased gradient and Hessian-vector estimators g(x,ξ),h(x,v,ξ) use IID samples of law P0, with joint sample law P. For every x,v, their integrable central moments satisfy EP0∥g−∇f(x)∥p≤σgp+αgp∥∇f(x)∥p and EP0∥h−∇2f(x)v∥q≤(σhq+αhq∥∇f(x)∥q)∥v∥q, where 1<p,q≤2. All scale parameters and Δ are nonnegative; ε>0. Target: a measurable returned point X with ∫∥∇f(X)∥dP≤ε. Costs count every gradient or HVP reply, including initialization, batches, guards and validation.

(1): extra ℓb+1(1+σg/R)b overhead on the common setup, and a large p-dependent prefactor.
(5) NSGD-Hess (Fradin et al. 2026), Theorem 5.1 Special case L1=αg=αh=0, additionally L2-Lipschitz Hessian and operator-norm Hessian moments. For fixed positive parameters as ε↓0: O(ε−max{b,2+b/q}). (1): removes Lipschitz-Hessian regularity, weakens operator-norm moments to directional HVP moments, and permits generalized curvature and affine noise. Matches the leading accuracy exponent on the overlap. (1): extra logarithms and (1+σg/R)b factors in shared stochastic terms.
(6) HystereticAffineHessianTransport (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(Dp,qλ[Ub+ΔJε−2⋅(Ub/q+(1+αg)2Ub−2)]). Here U=1+αg+σg/ε, J=L0+σh+(L1+αh)(ε+σg/(1+αg)), Dp,q=232b+16q/(q−1)(b+1), λ=1+log⁡(2+U+ΔJ/ε2+(R+σg)/ε).
(7) RanSOM-E (Chayti and Fakhouri 2026), Theorem B.24, Remark B.26; derived accuracy exponents O(ε−(b+1)) for q>p, Δ,L1,σg>0, remaining parameters fixed; O(ε−(2+b/q)) for q≤p. Includes batches and initialization. (6): O(ε−mλ) for q>p, m=max{b,2+b/q}<b+1. At p=3/2,q=2: ε−7/2λ instead of ε−4. Matches exponent for q≤p.
Relative to (1): linear Δ up to logs; λ replaces ℓb+1. For Δ=ε−a, a>0, fixed positive other parameters, exponents (1+a)m→a+m.		 (6): extra logarithm and large Dp,q; Euclidean scope versus general norms.
(8) RanSOM (Chayti and Fakhouri 2026), Corollary 4.8 / B.27; L1=αg=αh=0 O(1+(σg/ε)b+Δ(L0+σh)ε−2⋅[1+(σg/ε)b/q]). (6): Scope extends to generalized curvature and affine noise. (6): extra log. If b(1−1/q)>2, ΔL0≥σg2, σg≥ε, additional polynomial factor up to min{ΔL0/σg2,(σg/ε)b−2−b/q} (e.g. p<4/3,q=2).
(9) RanSOM-E (Chayti and Fakhouri 2026), Remark B.26; σg=0, derived bound O((1+αg)b[1+Δ(L0+σh)/ε2+Δ(L1+αh)/ε]). (6): matches polynomial accuracy dependence. Relative to (1), removes accuracy-dependent localization overhead when αg>0. (6): retains logarithm, Dp,q, and potentially larger αg dependence through (1+αg)b/q.

Abbr: HVP: Hessian-vector product; norms are Euclidean or their induced operator norms. b=p/(p−1), R=L0Δ+L1Δ+ε, S=σg+αgR, H=L0+σh+(L1+αh)R, Cp=2100b(1+b), and ℓ=1+log⁡(2+R/ε+ΔH/ε2+Δ/(εR)+S/ε). L2 denotes the Hessian Lipschitz constant. Asymptotic accuracy bounds hold with all other parameters fixed; other prior-work big-O constants may depend on p,q.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedAffineHessianVector

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  σg : ℝ
  αg : ℝ
  σh : ℝ
  αh : ℝ
  p : ℝ
  q : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Space (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)

abbrev spec : OracleTemplate.Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Space p → ℝ
  Query p := Space p × Option (Space p)
  Reply p := Space p
  Output p := Space p
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 ≤ p.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ p.L1 ∧
    0 ≤ p.σg ∧ 0 ≤ p.αg ∧ 0 ≤ p.σh ∧ 0 ≤ p.αh ∧
    1 < p.p ∧ p.p ≤ 2 ∧ 1 < p.q ∧ p.q ≤ 2 ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ∃ (g : Space p → p.Ω → Space p)
      (h : (Space p × Space p) → p.Ω → Space p)
      (P0 : ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → p.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → p.Ω) => ξ k) (P0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => p.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x, v) seed =>
            match v with
            | none => g x seed
            | some w => h (x, w) seed } ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    ContDiff ℝ 1 (gradient f) ∧
    (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x‖ ≤ p.L0 + p.L1 * ‖gradient f x‖) ∧
    (∃ m : ℝ, (∀ x, m ≤ f x) ∧ f p.x0 - m ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry h) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ p.p) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ p.p ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤
      p.σg ^ p.p + p.αg ^ p.p * ‖gradient f x‖ ^ p.p) ∧
    (∀ x v, Integrable (h (x, v)) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x v, ∫ ω, h (x, v) ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x v) ∧
    (∀ x v, Integrable (fun ω => ‖h (x, v) ω - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x v‖ ^ p.q)
      (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x v, ∫ ω, ‖h (x, v) ω - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x v‖ ^ p.q
      ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤
      (p.σh ^ p.q + p.αh ^ p.q * ‖gradient f x‖ ^ p.q) * ‖v‖ ^ p.q)
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedAffineHessianVector
